title: What If Your Heart Beat Only Twice a Minute? A Blue Whale's Does

scenes.text: What if your heart beat only twice a minute? A blue whale's can.
Stanford researchers stuck a sensor onto a wild blue whale off California.
During deep feeding dives, its heart slowed to as little as two beats a minute.
That was a third to a half lower than scientists had predicted for an animal that size.
Back at the surface, the heart sped up to roughly 25 to 37 beats a minute.
It weighs roughly 400 pounds, and it powers the largest animal that has ever lived.

description:
